articles.title: Tennis | US Open 2026 | Arthur Fery defends US Open preparation despite opening round exit to Lorenzo Musetti
articles.excerpt: Arthur Fery defends his US Open preparation after he lost in the opening round to Lorenzo Musetti in New York.
articles.content:
By Tony Fairbairn

  • Lorenzo Musetti [13] def Arthur Fery 6-3 6-3 7-5
  • Arthur Fery has defended his decision to play the week before the US Open after his straight sets defeat to Lorenzo Musetti.

 

It was not to be for Arthur Fery as the Wimbledon semi-finalist lost in straight sets to Lorenzo Musetti in the opening round of the US Open.

There was plenty of optimism for Fery who reached his maiden ATP final of his career in Winston-Salem the week prior.

However, he was up against a former Grand Slam semi-finalist in the form of Musetti who was starting to regain his form after a tough year.

It was a positive start for Fery who was proactive and aggressive on return as he kept the games close in the early stages.

Despite being under some pressure early on, Musetti was clinical on serve and fended off any early pressure from the Brit.

That would be a turning point in the opening set as Musetti broke in the last two return games to take the opening set 6-3.

In the second set, Fery made a really good start once again as he was clinical on serve as he used great variety to force errors from Musetti.

However, Musetti once again was able to raise his level when it mattered most and he broke serve for a 4-2 lead.

There was an immediate response from Fery though who was effective on return and he created four break points in the following game.

Once again Fery lacked that clinical touch when needed and Musetti fought off the break points before closing out a two sets to love lead with a hold to love.

It was a mountain to climb for Fery but the Brit remained positive and broke in the second game for a 2-0 lead.

There was a lack of consistency on the Fery serve though and the Brit was broken in two consecutive service games as Musetti took control of the contest.

A brief lifeline for Fery was obtained after he saved match point, the Brit broke Musetti when he was serving for the match.

The lifeline didn’t last long as Musetti won the last two games of the match to secure his place into the second round.

After the match Fery praised his Italian opponent for the way he played as he lost in the opening round.

“Tough match,” Fery was quoted by the LTA website as saying.

“Tough match,” Fery was quoted by the LTA website as saying.

“Obviously a good player that I faced. I didn’t have much time to get used to the site and the conditions coming straight from Winston-Salem, but I knew that coming in. I did what I could with what I had today.

“Not a great performance my end, but I have to give credit to Musetti. He’s tricky to play, has a one-hander, slices a lot and I wasn’t able to do enough. It’s useful for sure (competing against players of that level). I know what I have to work on, I have a lot of ideas coming straight off the court of what I could do better.

“My serve let me down today, which is not usually the case. When you play guys of that level it’s tough and the margins are small.”

 

 

Fery defends Winston-Salem decision after US Open exit

It wasn’t to be for Fery who would have been disappointed to exit the US Open at such an early stage.

Especially as he reached the final at Winston-Salem the week before which could have led to some fatigue for Fery.

However, the British number two has defended his decision to play the week before the US Open.

“The Grand Slams are the biggest tournaments, and everyone has their eye on them, but these past two weeks, would I sign on for that again? Yeah, probably to be honest,” Fery confessed to the LTA website.

“The Grand Slams are the biggest tournaments, and everyone has their eye on them, but these past two weeks, would I sign on for that again? Yeah, probably to be honest,” Fery confessed to the LTA website.

“I got a lot of ranking points, made an ATP final, which is good, even though it meant my preparation for the US Open wasn’t great.”

Now attention turns to the Davis Cup for Fery against Ecuador in London and Fery is excited about representing his country again.

“It’s going to be great, I’m really looking forward to that,” Fery claimed to the LTA website.

“It’s going to be great, I’m really looking forward to that,” Fery claimed to the LTA website.

“I’m looking forward to going back, practicing and getting in good shape to represent my country. Playing as the No.1 Brit at home is going to be special. It’s an honour to be No.1 in Great Britain and following all those names and great players who have had unbelievable careers. I’m new to it, and I’m just going to try and focus on the tennis.

“I’m going to go to Asia after Davis Cup, play tour events there for the first time. Go to Tokyo and then Shanghai, and then unsure yet. Hopefully I’ll play a busy schedule, get a lot of matches in, and hopefully qualify for Davis Cup Finals.”

The Davis Cup tie at the Copper Box Arena takes place on Saturday 19th of September and Sunday 20th of September.

articles.title: Katy Perry on How She Fell for Justin Trudeau and Manifested Their 'True Love'
articles.excerpt: Katy Perry opened up in a new interview about how her relationship with Justin Trudeau unfolded following her breakup from Orlando Bloom.
articles.content:
The singer opened up in a new interview about how her relationship with Trudeau unfolded.

THE RUNDOWN

  • Katy Perry opened up about how she fell in love with former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau in a new interview.
  • She called him the love of her life and detailed how she literally manifested their relationship.
  • The singer spoke adoringly about him, calling him “heart-centered” after spending their summer together.

Over a year into dating former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau, Katy Perry knows he’s the love of her life. She spoke to People about how she fell in love with him and why she believes she manifested the “epic legendary love” they now share.

On July 3, 2025, Perry and her ex-fiancé Orlando Bloom, who share 6-year-old Daisy, announced their split in a statement. At that point, Perry was in Australia for her Lifetimes Tour. “It was probably the hardest time,” she said. “My friends were all hanging out back home. I was crying and just feeling far away. But then my angels went to work. They really showed up.”

Perry and Trudeau were first seen on a date in Montreal on July 28, two days before her concert in the city. “I got to meet Justin on tour, and then things shifted,” she explained. That August, Perry wrote a list of things she was manifesting. She read the last item to People: “No. 10 just says, ‘True Love.’ And I think that’s where we’re at.”

Her relationship with Bloom ran its course, she explained: “I wouldn’t have stayed in something for nine years if there wasn’t really important things to learn. Each relationship is a teacher, right? I had to let it go so I could move forward. I always wanted this epic legendary love, and I was talking to my therapist about it: Everything in my life is epic, but this is kind of the missing puzzle piece—then it showed up.”

Trudeau has been one of her most supportive partners, attending 10 of her 20 shows this summer. “He knows the words, he’s supportive, and he’s in awe; it’s super healing,” she said. “He is really heart-centered, and I think that we align in that way. I’m so grateful.”

articles.title: iShares Core MSCI World ETF: SanDisk-Aufnahme treibt Quartals-Rebalancing - Börse Global
articles.excerpt: Die MSCI-Anpassung lenkt Milliardenströme in neue Titel. SanDisk profitiert, während Strategy ein Ausschlussverfahren für Dezember 2026 abwehrt.
articles.content:
Die MSCI-Anpassung lenkt Milliardenströme in neue Titel. SanDisk profitiert, während Strategy ein Ausschlussverfahren für Dezember 2026 abwehrt.

  • SanDisk erhält zusätzlichen passiven Kapitalzufluss
  • LG Innotek rückt in Südkoreas Index
  • NSE meldet Rekordumsatz in Schlussauktion
  • Strategy droht möglicher Ausschluss im Dezember

Die weltweite Neugewichtung der MSCI-Indizes hat am gestrigen Dienstag zu massiven Umschichtungen in passiven Anlageprodukten geführt. Mit dem Wirksamwerden der vierteljährlichen Überprüfung passt auch der iShares Core MSCI World UCITS ETF seine Bestände an die veränderte Zusammensetzung des Referenzindex an.

Während neue Schwergewichte aus dem Technologie- und Halbleitersektor aufrücken, mussten insbesondere Titel aus Schwellenländern und der Industrie ihre Plätze räumen.

SanDisk und Technologie-Titel im Fokus

Ein wesentlicher Treiber der aktuellen Anpassung ist die Aufnahme von SanDisk in den MSCI USA Index. Das Unternehmen profitierte zuletzt von einer starken Nachfrage nach Enterprise-SSDs für KI-Infrastrukturen.

Laut Daten von TrendForce stieg der Umsatz der fünf größten Anbieter in diesem Segment im zweiten Quartal 2026 um 103,6 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorquartal. SanDisk allein verzeichnete in diesem Zeitraum ein Umsatzwachstum von 102,9 Prozent auf 2,98 Milliarden US-Dollar. Die Aufnahme in den Index löste gestern signifikante Zuflüsse durch passive Fonds aus.

Parallel dazu gab es in den asiatischen Teilmärkten deutliche Verschiebungen. In Südkorea rückte LG Innotek neu in den Index auf, was Schätzungen zufolge Zuflüsse von bis zu 400 Milliarden KRW nach sich zog. Im Gegenzug wurden Werte wie LG Display und POSCO International aus dem Standard-Index entfernt. Diese Rotationen spiegeln die aktuelle Strategie wider, Unternehmen mit hohem Engagement in der KI-Lieferkette stärker zu gewichten.

Handelsrekorde und regulatorische Spannungen

Der Umfang der Umschichtungen zeigte sich besonders deutlich an der National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Indien. Die Schlussauktion am Montag verzeichnete einen Rekordumsatz von 39.718 Crore Rupien, was etwa 22 Prozent des gesamten Tagesumsatzes entsprach.

Marktbeobachter werten dies als erfolgreichen Belastungstest für die neuen Auktionsverfahren bei Index-Anpassungen. In Indonesien hingegen sorgte die Streichung des Technologieunternehmens GOTO für Verkaufsdruck, da der Titel aufgrund geringer Liquidität eine Sonderbehandlung bei der Preisstellung erhielt.

Abseits der faktischen Änderungen belastet eine Debatte um digitale Vermögenswerte die künftige Zusammensetzung. Der Softwarehersteller Strategy wehrt sich derzeit gegen einen Vorschlag des Indexanbieters, Unternehmen mit einem Bestand von mehr als 50 Prozent an digitalen Assets als „nicht-operativ“ einzustufen und damit auszuschließen.

Die Analysten von JPMorgan warnen in diesem Zusammenhang vor potenziellen Abflüssen in Höhe von 2,8 Milliarden US-Dollar, sollte ein Ausschluss im Dezember 2026 tatsächlich umgesetzt werden. Eine endgültige Entscheidung wird bis zum 16. Oktober erwartet.

Einordnung für Anleger

Für den iShares Core MSCI World UCITS ETF bedeutet die Umsetzung dieser Änderungen eine Beibehaltung der aktuellen Kursnähe zu wichtigen Trendlinien. Das Papier notiert mit einem Kurs von 126,25 Euro nahezu exakt auf seinem 50-Tage-Durchschnitt, der Abstand beträgt lediglich -0,005 Prozent. Trotz der jüngsten Volatilität in einzelnen Sektoren weist der ETF seit Jahresbeginn eine positive Entwicklung von 13 Prozent auf.

Anleger beobachten zudem die kommenden Wochen genau, da neben den MSCI-Änderungen auch andere Indexanbieter ihre Zusammensetzung korrigieren. So wird Volkswagen zum 21. September den Euro Stoxx 50 verlassen müssen, während Unternehmen wie Nokia und Engie aufrücken. Diese kumulierten Verschiebungen in den großen Leitindizes zwingen passive Großinvestoren weiterhin zu einer präzisen Abstimmung ihrer Portfoliogewichte, um den Tracking Error zu minimieren.
